q: How do I cancel a train ticket?
tags: cancel cancellation refund return money
a: Reserved e-tickets can be cancelled from the account you booked with. The refund depends on the class and how long before departure you cancel. Check the official IRCTC/Indian Railways refund rules for current charges.

q: What is Tatkal booking?
tags: tatkal urgent last minute emergency quota
a: Tatkal is a last-minute quota that usually opens one day before the journey (excluding the journey date) at a higher fare. Seats are limited and sell out quickly.

q: What do WL, RAC and CNF mean?
tags: waiting list wl rac cnf confirmed status berth
a: CNF means confirmed. RAC (Reservation Against Cancellation) lets you board and share a berth until one frees up. WL (waiting list) tickets are confirmed only if others cancel.

q: What is a PNR number?
tags: pnr booking reference status check
a: The PNR is a 10-digit Passenger Name Record number printed on your ticket. Use it to check booking and seat status.

q: How much luggage can I carry?
tags: luggage baggage bags weight limit allowance
a: Each class has a free luggage allowance, and higher AC classes allow more. Extra luggage should be booked at the parcel/luggage office before the journey.

q: Can I get food on the train?
tags: food meal pantry catering eat order
a: Many long-distance trains have a pantry car, and premium trains often include meals in the fare. You can also pre-order meals for delivery at stations through e-catering services.

q: Which travel class should I choose?
tags: class sleeper 3a 2a 1a chair car ac difference comfort
a: Sleeper (SL) is the cheapest reserved class. AC 3 Tier (3A) balances comfort and cost. AC 2 Tier (2A) has more space and curtains. AC First (1A) offers private cabins. AC Chair Car (CC) has seats for daytime trips.

q: What is the difference between Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Duronto?
tags: rajdhani shatabdi duronto premium train types
a: Rajdhani trains are fast overnight AC trains linking state capitals to Delhi. Shatabdi trains are fast daytime chair-car trains. Duronto trains run with very few stops. All three usually include meals and cost more.

q: How does RailMate rank journeys?
tags: score ranking recommend how does it work algorithm
a: Each journey gets four sub-scores out of 100: speed (average km/h), cost (fare compared with a standard express fare), reliability (chance of arriving on time) and convenience (transfers, night departures, long layovers). Your priority setting changes how these are weighted.

q: What does the delay risk mean?
tags: delay risk late probability prediction punctuality
a: It is the estimated chance of arriving more than 30 minutes late, from a machine-learning model. The bundled model is trained on synthetic labels, so treat it as a demonstration rather than a real forecast.

q: Where does RailMate's train data come from?
tags: data source dataset accurate current timetable
a: RailMate uses the public DataMeet Indian Railways dataset (CC0 licence), a historical snapshot from around 2016-17. Timings, train numbers and station codes may have changed, so always confirm on official channels before travelling.

q: Why can't I find a station?
tags: station missing not found code search renamed
a: Search by station name or code. Some stations were renamed after the dataset was collected, e.g. Mumbai CST appears with its old code CSTM. Stations with no train halts in the data are hidden.

q: Are the fares shown exact?
tags: fare price cost exact official estimate
a: No. Fares are estimates from a distance-based model with class and train-type surcharges. Official fares, dynamic pricing and concessions can differ.

q: What is a connecting journey?
tags: connection transfer change trains layover
a: When no direct train fits, RailMate combines two trains with a change at an intermediate station. Layovers are kept between 45 minutes and 6 hours, and the missed-connection risk is shown.

q: What is missed connection risk?
tags: missed connection risk layover short
a: It estimates the chance that a delay on the first train makes you miss the second. Short layovers carry more risk, and the estimate grows with the first train's delay probability.

q: How do I save a trip?
tags: save trip my trips account bookmark plan
a: Create a free RailMate account, search for a journey and press 'Save trip'. Saved trips appear under My Trips. Saving a trip is not a ticket booking.

q: Can I book tickets on RailMate?
tags: book ticket booking buy purchase
a: No. RailMate is a planning tool. Book tickets through official Indian Railways channels such as IRCTC.

q: What is the senior citizen concession?
tags: senior citizen concession discount elderly
a: Concession rules for senior citizens have changed over time. Please check the current rules on the official Indian Railways website.

q: What is a general (unreserved) ticket?
tags: general unreserved gn ticket counter uts
a: A general ticket allows travel in unreserved coaches without a berth or seat reservation. These tickets can be bought at station counters or through the UTS app.

q: How early should I reach the station?
tags: reach early arrive station time before departure
a: Reaching 30-45 minutes early is usually sensible, more at large stations or during festivals. This gives time for security checks and finding your platform and coach.

q: Can I change my boarding station?
tags: change boarding point station
a: Reserved tickets generally allow a change of boarding point within the rules and time limits. Check the official rules before your journey.

q: What happens if my train is cancelled?
tags: train cancelled cancellation by railways refund
a: If the railway cancels a train, reserved e-tickets are generally refunded automatically. Check your booking account for the refund status.

q: Do I need ID while travelling?
tags: id proof identity aadhaar document ticket checking
a: Passengers on reserved tickets are generally required to carry a valid photo ID matching the ticket. Check the list of accepted documents on the official website.

q: Is there a limit on passengers per booking?
tags: passengers limit group how many
a: Online bookings limit passengers per ticket, with different limits for regular and Tatkal bookings. RailMate trip plans allow up to 6 passengers.

q: Why does a train show 'running days not in source data'?
tags: running days weekly daily runs on which days
a: The public dataset does not include running days, so RailMate cannot confirm them for most trains. Where running days are known (loaded from data/running_days.csv) they are enforced in search.
